title: Neural Simulation-Based Inference for Computational Cognitive Models: A Tutorial
abstract: arXiv:2611.17608v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Computational cognitive modeling is an increasingly essential methodology to elucidate the mechanisms underlying human and animal cognition. By fitting models to empirical data, researchers can perform parameter estimation, model comparison, and model-based neural analyses to assess competing theories, quantify individual differences, and investigate neural representations. Typically, fitting these models relies on likelihood-dependent methods (e.g., Maximum likelihood estimation or hierarchical Bayesian methods). However, for many reasonable cognitive models, computing the likelihood is computationally intractable, in which case these methods become inadequate. This substantially limits the range of theories that researchers can investigate. translated_title: 面向计算认知模型的神经仿真推断：一篇教程
translated_abstract: 计算认知建模是一种日益重要的方法论，用于阐明人类与动物认知背后的机制。通过将模型拟合到实证数据，研究者可以进行参数估计、模型比较以及基于模型的神经分析，以评估相互竞争的理论、量化个体差异并研究神经表征。通常，拟合这些模型依赖于依赖似然函数的方法（例如最大似然估计或分层贝叶斯方法）。然而，对于许多合理的认知模型而言，计算似然函数在计算上是难以实现的，在这种情况下这些方法便不再适用。这极大地限制了研究者可以考察的理论范围。基于神经网络的仿真推断（neural SBI）已成为克服这一障碍的强大工具包，其通过在由模型仿真生成的数据集上训练深度神经网络……
tldr: 这篇教程介绍了神经仿真推断（neural SBI）如何通过在模型仿真数据上训练深度神经网络，克服计算认知模型中似然函数不可计算的问题，从而突破传统拟合方法的局限、拓展可研究的认知理论范围。
en_tdlr: This tutorial presents neural simulation-based inference (neural SBI), which trains deep neural networks on simulated data to overcome intractable likelihoods in computational cognitive models, expanding the range of cognitive theories that researchers can investigate.
